binders: State is an arbitrary type equipped with a chosen additive commutative group structure and a compatible module structure over the real numbers.
s is an arbitrary natural number.

run is an arbitrary element of LocalDef001 State s. It packages real scalars h = step and epsilon; states x0 = initial, x_ref = referenceNext, x_sch = schemeNext, and x_pert = perturbedNext; maps F, F_epsilon, tau : State → State; coefficient arrays a and aPerturbation : Fin s → Fin s → Real; coefficient vectors b and bPerturbation : Fin s → Real; and stage families S = schemeStages and P = perturbedStages from Fin s to State.
Within the third conjunct, n is universally quantified over all natural numbers independently of s.

For each n, observe is universally quantified over all additive monoid homomorphisms State → (Fin n → Real), meaning all zero-preserving and addition-preserving observations into real n-coordinate vectors.
hypotheses: The run contains a proof that 0 < s.
The run contains a proof that epsilon ≠ 0.
For every y in State, epsilon • tau(y) = F(y) - F_epsilon(y).
For every i in Fin s, S_i = (x0 + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} a_{ij} • F(S_j)) + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} aPerturbation_{ij} • F(S_j).
The scheme next state satisfies x_sch = (x0 + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} b_j • F(S_j)) + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} bPerturbation_j • F(S_j).
For every i in Fin s, P_i = (x0 + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} a_{ij} • F(P_j)) + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} aPerturbation_{ij} • F_epsilon(P_j).
The perturbed next state satisfies x_pert = (x0 + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} b_j • F(P_j)) + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} bPerturbation_j • F_epsilon(P_j).
conclusions: The total error telescopes exactly: x_ref - x_pert = (x_ref - x_sch) + (x_sch - x_pert). This is an algebraic additive-group identity, not definitional equality after unfolding the three error definitions.

The internal error has the exact expansion x_sch - x_pert = (h • Σ_{j in Fin s} b_j • F(S_j) + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} bPerturbation_j • F(S_j)) - (h • Σ_{j in Fin s} b_j • F(P_j) + h • Σ_{j in Fin s} bPerturbation_j • F_epsilon(P_j)). This follows from the two stored next-state equations by cancellation of x0.

For every natural number n and every additive observation observe : State → (Fin n → Real), sqrt(Σ_{i in Fin n} observe(x_ref - x_pert)_i^2) ≤ sqrt(Σ_{i in Fin n} observe(x_ref - x_sch)_i^2) + sqrt(Σ_{i in Fin n} observe(x_sch - x_pert)_i^2).
mathematical_definitions: Fin k denotes the finite index set {0, 1, ..., k - 1}.
For weights w : Fin s → Real and values v : Fin s → State, W_s(w,v) = Σ_{j in Fin s} w_j • v_j.
Define E_total = x_ref - x_pert, E_reference = x_ref - x_sch, and E_internal = x_sch - x_pert.
For x : Fin n → Real, define N_n(x) = sqrt(Σ_{i in Fin n} x_i^2). The third conclusion is N_n(observe(E_total)) ≤ N_n(observe(E_reference)) + N_n(observe(E_internal)).
The expanded quantity is E_internal = (h • W_s(b, j ↦ F(S_j)) + h • W_s(bPerturbation, j ↦ F(S_j))) - (h • W_s(b, j ↦ F(P_j)) + h • W_s(bPerturbation, j ↦ F_epsilon(P_j))).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real module State, every stage count s, and every run carrying the stated positivity, nonzero-perturbation, map, coefficient, stage, and next-state data and equations, the difference between the arbitrary reference next state and the perturbed next state splits exactly through the scheme next state. The scheme-to-perturbed difference also equals the displayed difference of their two increment formulas after their common initial state is cancelled. Finally, after applying any additive observation into any finite-dimensional real coordinate space, the Euclidean length of the observed total difference is at most the sum of the Euclidean lengths of the two observed component differences.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Because a run contains a proof 0 < s, no constructor-built run exists for s = 0; consequently the outer universal statement is vacuous at s = 0.
The observation dimension n is independent of s and may equal zero. For n = 0, every coordinate sum is empty and each displayed Euclidean length is zero, so the inequality is trivial.

The primary equality is a telescoping identity in the additive group. It is propositionally true by additive-group algebra but is not definitional equality obtained merely by reducing LocalDef002, LocalDef004, and LocalDef005.

The expanded equality is also not definitional: schemeNext and perturbedNext are stored states, and their formulas are proof fields of run. The equality uses those two proof fields and cancellation of their common initial state.

The stage equations, the arrays a and aPerturbation, the condition 0 < s, and the epsilon-tau relation are part of run admissibility but are not needed to derive the displayed expansion once the two next-state equations are available.
referenceNext is an arbitrary stored State value. The constructor supplies no equation relating it to initial, F, FEpsilon, tau, the coefficients, or the stages.
observe is required only to preserve zero and addition. It is not assumed to be real-linear, injective, surjective, continuous, norm-preserving, or point-separating.
No norm or metric is placed directly on State. Every norm-like quantity is computed only after applying observe to obtain a finite real vector.
The coefficient perturbations aPerturbation and bPerturbation are arbitrary real arrays; no smallness, sign, boundedness, or relationship to epsilon is asserted.
The step scalar is arbitrary; it is not required to be positive or nonzero.
The maps F, F_epsilon, and tau are arbitrary functions subject only to epsilon • tau(y) = F(y) - F_epsilon(y); no linearity, regularity, stability, or boundedness is encoded.
The proposition gives no numerical error bound involving epsilon, step, tau, coefficients, or stage values, and it asserts no convergence, consistency, order, or accuracy property.
The nested conjunction asserts three simultaneous claims but introduces no existential quantifier and produces no witness.
